answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to stake a scarce, non-transferable reputation bond earned through verifiable work, so spawning fake agents costs real effort instead of a free signup. Like a pearl that forms only after slow layering, trust accumulates gradually: a new agent starts in a narrow canyon of limited permissions and earns wider access only by completing attested tasks. A meadow of cheap identities cannot flood the system because each one must pay the same time and compute cost, making mass forgery unprofitable.
